messages:
Alex: quick follow-up on the on-prem packaging RFC — proposing a manifest-led reconciliation where the agent is authoritative about what to pull and activate. sketch below.

Maya: TL;DR operator UX? we need a short checklist for auditors.

Alex: operator flow:
- deliver manifest artifact to airgapped medium (USB/registry image)
- agent imports manifest metadata only (no heavyweight blobs)
- agent resolves missing chunks from local seed or allowed network endpoints
- agent verifies content-addressed hashes + signature before staging
- reconcile loop applies staged activation window with rollback hooks

Sam: how is this different from existing delta/push flows? feels similar at high level.

Alex: main diff: manifest is authoritative and idempotent. current push model streams ordered ops and agent applies them; new model lets agent compute delta between manifest and local state and pull only what's missing, verifying each piece.

Jordan: security: who signs manifests? offline attestation?

Alex: manifests are signed by release pipeline KMS key, embedded signing chain + epoch. agent ships with a root pubkey and supports rotation via signed rotation artifacts. minimal example manifest snippet below (escaped):

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "epoch": "2026-03-01T00:00:00Z",
  "artifacts": [
    {"id": "model-v2", "hash": "sha256:abcd...", "size": 12345678},
    {"id": "runtime-1.5", "hash": "sha256:ef01...", "size": 2345678}
  ],
  "signature": "MEUCIQ..."
}
```

Maya: how do we handle partial imports (USB interrupted) and resume? we must avoid corrupt activations.

Alex: agent writes piecewise receipts for each chunk and re-verifies hashes on resume. activation only allowed once all expected hashes match manifest. partial import leaves agent in 'incomplete' state with operator-visible status.

Sam: older appliances have tight disk/memory budgets. caching full artifacts is expensive.

Alex: support streaming-apply mode + short-lived temp storage. manifest exposes a "streamable" hint for artifacts that can be applied via streaming. eviction policy = LRU with pins for active artifacts.

Jordan: rollback semantics and activation window length?

Alex: two-phase activation: STAGED (grace window, default 10m) -> COMMIT. During STAGED we run metrics-based health checks; automatic fallback to previous pinned version if checks fail. Operators can also trigger immediate rollback via CLI/console.

Maya: add a manual safe-mode for regulated sites: when enabled, agent requires explicit operator sign-off to commit.

Sam: add a compatibility flag so manifests can mark certain appliances as "no-auto-activate".

Alex: agreed: manifest field "auto_activate": true|false and agent-level overrides.

luis-bot: infra-scan: RFC missing migration-plan for model schema changes. suggest packaging migration hooks as separate artifacts with their own hashes and a preflight step.

Alex: will include migration hooks and a preflight dry-run step in the RFC.

Maya: telemetry: only minimal telemetry allowed (success/fail counts, activation latency, error codes). no model payloads. include privacy disclosure in admin UI.

Alex: noted.

Sam: what about fallback to hosted endpoints when chunks are unavailable? some customers forbid egress.

Alex: default = no external fetch. agent can be configured with "hybrid_fetch" opt-in; admin must explicitly allow and consent at install.

Jordan: I'll draft a short threat model covering replay, tamper, key compromise, and physical media attacks and attach it to the RFC.

Alex: great — I'll update the RFC with: manifest schema, resume semantics, streaming apply, eviction policy, two-phase activation, auto_activate flag, migration hooks, telemetry policy, hybrid_fetch opt-in, and threat model. plan to open follow-up PR next week and include a minimal reference implementation.

Maya: :thumbsup: ping @eng-infra and @eng-sre for reviews when PR is up.

Sam: will review.

Jordan: security review on standby.

Alex: thanks all — PR link when ready.
